item.title: City of Milton offices closed for Thanksgiving; sanitation schedule adjusted
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton will close all municipal offices Thursday, November 26, and Friday, November 27, for the Thanksgiving holiday, the city announced Monday. Residents should plan ahead for sanitation services, which will operate on an adjusted schedule that week. Regular pickups will continue Monday and Tuesday, but no collections will be made…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton will close all municipal offices Thursday, November 26, and Friday, November 27, for the Thanksgiving holiday, the city announced Monday.

Residents should plan ahead for sanitation services, which will operate on an adjusted schedule that week. Regular pickups will continue Monday and Tuesday, but no collections will be made Wednesday through Friday. The city reminds residents they will receive only one sanitation pickup the following week.

City offices will resume normal business hours Monday, November 30. For details, residents can contact the City of Milton at (850) 983-5400 or PIO@miltonfl.org.

item.title: House Passes Major Veterans Benefits Legislation; Patronis Says Work Isn't Finished
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Legislation that could change retirement and disability benefits for thousands of combat-injured veterans is moving forward in Congress, with Northwest Florida Congressman Jimmy Patronis expressing optimism about its prospects. The U.S. House voted 392 to 18 Thursday to approve the Major Richard Star Act, which…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Legislation that could change retirement and disability benefits for thousands of combat-injured veterans is moving forward in Congress, with Northwest Florida Congressman Jimmy Patronis expressing optimism about its prospects.

The U.S. House voted 392 to 18 Thursday to approve the Major Richard Star Act, which would allow certain medically retired veterans to receive both military retirement pay and Department of Veterans Affairs disability compensation without the reduction currently required under federal law.

The legislation is particularly significant for service members who were forced to retire because of combat-related injuries before completing 20 years of military service.

During an interview Monday on NewsRadio 92.3, Patronis discussed the legislation's importance for veterans whose military careers were cut short by serious injuries.

"Now they'll be eligible for their VA benefits and also their federal retirement," Patronis said, while emphasizing that the change depends on the bill passing the Senate and receiving the president's signature.

The House also approved the broader Take Care of America's Veterans Act on Veterans Day. That package includes a modified version of the Major Richard Star Act, along with additional provisions addressing veterans' health care, benefits, caregivers and surviving spouses.

Not everyone agrees on the broader package. Veterans organizations and lawmakers have raised concerns about some of its provisions, even while supporting expanded benefits for combat-injured retirees.

Both measures still require further congressional action.

For Northwest Florida, home to a substantial military and veteran population, the legislation could have a direct financial impact on eligible veterans and their families.

No changes to retirement or disability payments have taken effect as a result of the House votes.

item.title: Pensacola Man Federally Indicted for Allegedly Threatening President Trump
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A Pensacola man is facing federal criminal charges after prosecutors say he made online threats against President Donald Trump. Steven Richard Hutchings, 37, has been indicted on two counts of threatening the president, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Florida. The charges stem…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A Pensacola man is facing federal criminal charges after prosecutors say he made online threats against President Donald Trump.

Steven Richard Hutchings, 37, has been indicted on two counts of threatening the president, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Florida.

The charges stem from statements Hutchings allegedly made online in September 2025.

According to court documents described in local reporting, the statements included threats of violence directed at the president.

Hutchings has already made his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Hope Thai Cannon at the federal courthouse in Pensacola.

A jury trial is scheduled to begin December 14, 2026, before U.S. District Judge M. Casey Rodgers.

The investigation was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations, with federal prosecutors handling the case.

If convicted, Hutchings faces a maximum possible sentence of ten years in federal prison on each count.

The U.S. Attorney's Office emphasized that an indictment represents allegations made by a grand jury. It is not evidence of guilt.

Hutchings is presumed innocent unless and until prosecutors establish guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

The case is among the latest federal criminal proceedings being handled in the Northern District of Florida.

item.title: UWF Announces $100,000 in Hurricane Recovery Grants for Military-Owned Businesses
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Military-connected small business owners in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties may be eligible for new financial assistance as they continue recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The University of West Florida announced Monday that Navy Federal Credit Union has provided $100,000 to establish a small business recovery…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Military-connected small business owners in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties may be eligible for new financial assistance as they continue recovering from Hurricane Isaias.

The University of West Florida announced Monday that Navy Federal Credit Union has provided $100,000 to establish a small business recovery grant program.

The initiative will be administered in partnership with the Florida Small Business Development Center at UWF.

Eligible businesses can apply for grants of up to $5,000 to help cover expenses directly related to hurricane damage.

Those expenses can include building repairs, replacement equipment, inventory, cleanup, temporary operating space, utility restoration, and insurance deductibles.

Kelly Massey, regional director of the Florida SBDC at UWF, said the assistance is intended to help military-connected business owners rebuild and continue contributing to the local economy.

To qualify, businesses must be located in Escambia or Santa Rosa County and be at least 51 percent owned by qualifying veterans, active-duty military members, or spouses of active-duty service members.

Applicants must also meet financial and operating-history requirements.

Businesses must have generated less than $1 million in sales during 2025, been operating by December 31, 2025, and filed their 2025 federal business tax returns.

They must also document physical damage to business property or assets caused by Hurricane Isaias.

The grants are intended for locally owned, privately held, for-profit businesses.

Applications opened Monday, November 16, and will remain available until 5 p.m. November 30.

Business owners can review the complete eligibility requirements and apply through the Florida SBDC at UWF's hurricane recovery grant page.

item.title: Investigation Continues After Mississippi Homicide Suspect Shot by Escambia Deputies
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: ESCAMBIA COUNTY, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Investigators are continuing to examine a deputy-involved shooting at a Pensacola-area motel Friday afternoon involving a man wanted in connection with a homicide investigation in Mississippi. The confrontation happened at the Sweet Dreams Inn on Plantation Road. The suspect has been identified as Richard…
item.content:encoded:
ESCAMBIA COUNTY, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Investigators are continuing to examine a deputy-involved shooting at a Pensacola-area motel Friday afternoon involving a man wanted in connection with a homicide investigation in Mississippi.

The confrontation happened at the Sweet Dreams Inn on Plantation Road.

The suspect has been identified as Richard Timothy Ward, who was being sought by authorities in Long Beach, Mississippi.

Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons said deputies and Florida Highway Patrol troopers received information that Ward might be staying in a room at the motel.

Deputies approached the room and encountered the suspect, who allegedly produced a firearm.

"He fired once at us, and three of our deputies returned fire to him, striking him," Simmons said in a video statement released shortly after the shooting.

The sheriff said none of the deputies were injured.

Ward was struck by gunfire and transported for medical treatment.

The incident followed the discovery of two women dead inside a home in Long Beach, Mississippi, earlier Friday.

Authorities initially described the case as a possible double homicide. However, the Harrison County coroner subsequently clarified that one death appeared to be from natural causes, while the other was being investigated as a homicide.

The women were identified as 84-year-old Doris Crimmins and 63-year-old Kimberly Hernandez, the suspect's mother and sister.

Mississippi authorities said autopsies were scheduled to determine the circumstances of the deaths.

The shooting in Escambia County is subject to a separate investigation into the deputies' use of force.

The investigation remains ongoing, and the circumstances described by the sheriff have not yet been independently established in court.

item.title: Joe Vinson Wins Escambia County Commission Seat by Just 19 Votes
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- After one of the closest local elections in recent memory, Joe Vinson is preparing to take his seat on the Escambia County Commission. The non-party-affiliated challenger defeated Republican incumbent Ashlee Hofberger by just 19 votes in the District 4 race. Final certified results show Vinson receiving 13,096…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- After one of the closest local elections in recent memory, Joe Vinson is preparing to take his seat on the Escambia County Commission.

The non-party-affiliated challenger defeated Republican incumbent Ashlee Hofberger by just 19 votes in the District 4 race.

Final certified results show Vinson receiving 13,096 votes to Hofberger's 13,077. The candidates were separated by less than one-tenth of a percentage point.

The race remained unsettled for more than a week after Election Day as election officials conducted recounts and processed additional ballots, including those from military personnel and Americans living overseas.

When the final results were announced Friday, Vinson thanked his supporters while acknowledging the nearly half of District 4 voters who had supported Hofberger.

"Never let anyone tell you that your vote doesn't count. Every single vote mattered in this case," Vinson said.

Vinson also pledged to work toward earning the trust of voters who did not support him.

His victory makes him the first candidate without a party affiliation elected to the Escambia County Commission.

During a Monday morning interview on NewsRadio 92.3, Vinson discussed priorities including greater transparency in county government, making county information easier for residents to access, and improving communication with constituents.

He has also identified hurricane debris cleanup and the county's financial challenges as issues requiring attention.

Vinson is scheduled to take office Tuesday, November 17, as the new District 4 commissioner.

The election results underscore just how much individual votes can matter in a closely contested local race.

item.title: Florida execution warrant signed for 1998 child murder case
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Gov. Ron DeSantis has signed an execution warrant for a man convicted in a 1998 child killing, marking what would be the 22nd execution carried out in Florida this year, according to reporting from North Escambia. The development comes as a group of death row exonerees has appealed to Florida's next governor to reconsider the state's accelerated…
item.content:encoded:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has signed an execution warrant for a man convicted in a 1998 child killing, marking what would be the 22nd execution carried out in Florida this year, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The development comes as a group of death row exonerees has appealed to Florida's next governor to reconsider the state's accelerated pace of executions. The exonerated individuals, who spent years on death row before being released, have raised concerns about the speed at which capital sentences are being carried out.

Florida has become one of the nation's most active states in executing death row inmates, with the pace raising questions among criminal justice advocates about due process and the reliability of convictions in older cases.

item.title: Cold Front Brings Frost Risk, Sunny Skies to North Escambia This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom

After Thursday reaches a pleasant high near 74 degrees, temperatures will plummet for the remainder of the weekend. Friday and Saturday highs are expected to settle in the upper 50s…
item.content:encoded:
A cold front moving through North Escambia today will bring a significant shift in weather conditions, delivering dry skies and noticeably colder air by week's end.

After Thursday reaches a pleasant high near 74 degrees, temperatures will plummet for the remainder of the weekend. Friday and Saturday highs are expected to settle in the upper 50s and low 60s, with frost likely developing overnight as clear skies allow temperatures to drop further.

The dry, sunny conditions accompanying the cold front should provide ideal weather for outdoor activities during the day, though residents planning to spend time outside early mornings or evenings should prepare for much cooler conditions. Anyone with sensitive plants or outdoor preparations should take precautions against frost damage Friday and Saturday nights.

item.content:encoded: Matt Dannheisser, who has served as Century's town attorney for more than three decades, has stepped down effective immediately, citing difficulties with the municipality's senior leadership. According to reporting from North Escambia, Dannheisser's departure marks the end of a lengthy tenure representing the small North Escambia community. The town has already begun the process of bringing in interim legal counsel to fill the gap left by his resignation. Mayor Ben Boutwell and the five-member town council received Dannheisser's resignation letter via email. The specific nature of the workplace conflicts that prompted his exit was not detailed in the initial announcement, but the sudden nature of the departure and the swift move to find replacement counsel suggest the situation had become untenable for both sides.

item.title: Historic SS United States Departs for Final Voyage, Scuttled at Sea
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that carried presidents and celebrities across the Atlantic, departed Thursday for what will be its final resting place at the bottom of the sea. According to WKRG-TV 5, historians and former passengers gathered to bid farewell to the vessel as it left port, marking the end of an era for one of…
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that carried presidents and celebrities across the Atlantic, departed Thursday for what will be its final resting place at the bottom of the sea. According to WKRG-TV 5, historians and former passengers gathered to bid farewell to the vessel as it left port, marking the end of an era for one of America's most iconic ships.

The SS United States, which set the transatlantic speed record when it launched in 1952, has been a floating museum and tourist attraction in recent years. The decision to scuttle the ship—intentionally sinking it in a designated deepwater location—comes after efforts to preserve or repurpose the vessel proved economically unfeasible.

The ship's final voyage carries historical weight for those who sailed aboard her during her heyday and for maritime historians who viewed her as a symbol of American engineering and design. The scuttling process will turn the ship into an artificial reef, creating a new marine habitat while ending decades of uncertainty about the vessel's future.

item.title: Hundreds gather in Destin to bid farewell to historic SS United States

The ship, which sat anchored about 22 miles off the coast of Destin Harbor, drew onlookers determined to witness a piece of naval history before its fate is…
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of people lined up in Destin on Wednesday to catch a final glimpse of the SS United States, the iconic ocean liner that once represented the height of American maritime travel. The ship, which sat anchored about 22 miles off the coast of Destin Harbor, drew onlookers determined to witness a piece of naval history before its fate is decided.

The SS United States, launched in 1952, was a symbol of American engineering and luxury travel during the golden age of ocean liners. The vessel held the transatlantic speed record for decades and carried presidents, celebrities, and thousands of everyday passengers across the Atlantic.

According to WKRG News 5, the gathering reflected the emotional connection many people have to the historic ship. Despite the distance from shore and the wait involved in viewing the vessel, attendees showed up to say goodbye to a maritime landmark that represented an era of American innovation and elegance.

item.title: SS United States sunk off Florida panhandle to become world's largest artificial reef
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The SS United States, an iconic ocean liner, has been intentionally sunk off Florida's Gulf Coast to create the world's largest artificial reef, according to reports from CBS News and the Pensacola News Journal. The vessel, which was being scuttled off the coast of Florida's panhandle, completed its final journey Thursday as crews executed the…
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, an iconic ocean liner, has been intentionally sunk off Florida's Gulf Coast to create the world's largest artificial reef, according to reports from CBS News and the Pensacola News Journal.

The vessel, which was being scuttled off the coast of Florida's panhandle, completed its final journey Thursday as crews executed the controlled sinking. Officials confirmed the ship was fully submerged as part of the planned operation.

The project transforms the historic liner—once a symbol of American maritime travel—into a marine habitat that will support fish populations and diving tourism in the region. The artificial reef is expected to attract divers and support local marine ecosystems in the waters off Northwest Florida.
